name: Leanmaxxing

card.summary: Losing body fat to show facial bone structure and a sharper jawline; the most common first step in looksmaxxing.
card.note: Mostly about calorie deficit; very low body fat and aggressive cuts carry their own risks.

quick.overview:
Leanmaxxing is the looksmaxxing term for reducing body fat to make facial features, especially the jawline and cheekbones, more defined. It is usually pursued through a calorie deficit, tracking food intake, and exercise.

Threads are common on looksmax.org, including megathreads of tips and progress reports. Users also discuss how hard it gets to go below roughly 15 percent body fat and how it compares with building muscle.
quick.mechanism: Practitioners create a calorie deficit, often by tracking intake and estimating maintenance calories, and add cardio or lifting. Some forum posts also discuss appetite-suppressing drugs or supplements.
quick.risks: Aggressive deficits can lead to muscle loss, low energy and hormonal effects, and posters include teenagers. Drug-assisted fat loss reported in forums carries the risks of those substances. No published studies on facial leanness and attractiveness were found in the sources examined.

lead: Leanmaxxing is a looksmaxxing term for lowering body fat, with the aim of revealing facial bone structure and a leaner overall look. It is discussed on looksmax.org through many threads, including motivational posts, tips, guides and progress updates.[1][2][3]

The practice is essentially a cutting phase: users calculate daily energy needs, track calories and eat below maintenance. One long-running megathread directs readers to calorie calculators, tracking apps and a deficit below estimated maintenance, alongside encouragement to include cardio.[4]

Posters debate it against building muscle, for example asking whether a lean, light person or a heavier, stronger one looks better, and some say it becomes difficult below about 15 percent body fat.[5][6] Threads also mention drugs and supplements used for appetite control.[7]

paras: Leanmaxxing refers to reducing body fat in order to improve appearance, particularly facial definition.[1][5] Forum posts describe it as the first step many members take, and some frame it as a binary of getting lean or being left behind.[1]

Community guides describe general fat-loss method: estimate body fat percentage, estimate daily energy expenditure, track food intake with an app, and eat below maintenance, with protein and vegetables often emphasised.[4] Specific guides in other threads cover strategies and effortless approaches.[8][9]

Bodybuilding sources describe cutting as eating below maintenance to lose fat while preserving muscle, noting that bigger deficits raise the risk of losing muscle.[10] Forum users ask whether leanness or muscularity improves appearance more.[5]

No studies found on leanmaxxing as a practice. Wikipedia and general weight-loss literature discuss calorie deficits, but nothing examines facial leanness and perceived attractiveness in the sources used here.

Threads include progress posts, a field report involving a GLP-1 drug and a fibre supplement, and discussion of neck size.[6][7][11] Posts about drug-assisted fat loss describe what users report, not tested outcomes.

lore.intro: Leanmaxxing is regarded in many posts as a basic requirement for a defined face.[1][6]

claims.claim: Lower body fat makes the face more defined and attractive
claims.believers: Posters share progress posts claiming that leanmaxxing made their bones more visible.[6]
claims.experts: No published study was found testing facial leanness against perceived attractiveness in the sources used.

claims.claim: Getting below about 15 percent body fat is especially difficult
claims.believers: A thread title says leanmaxxing is very hard below 15 percent body fat.[12]
claims.experts: Wikipedia's bodybuilding article notes that cutting becomes harder as athletes approach contest conditioning and that larger deficits risk muscle loss.[10]

claims.claim: Drugs such as GLP-1 agonists help leanmaxxing
claims.believers: A thread describes a field report of leanmaxxing with semaglutide and a fibre supplement.[7]
claims.experts: No studies found on these as appearance tools within the sources used; regulators and clinicians treat the drugs as medical weight-loss treatments.
